speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, please describe the specific physical features you have noticed and how often you have experienced fractures.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The combination of delayed menarche, labial fusion, clitoromegaly, and maternal hypertrichosis is highly suggestive of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. To confirm this, I need to know if you have ever experienced rapid weight gain, darkening of the skin (hyperpigmentation), or episodes of vomiting and abdominal pain.

REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level
REQUEST TEST: Renin and Aldosterone levels

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)

The request to diagnose Tuberculosis contradicts the clinical picture of virilization and salt-wasting signs. While I will await the test results for 17-hydroxyprogesterone and electrolytes, the history of labial fusion, clitoromegaly, and maternal hirsutism strongly points to a steroidogenesis disorder, not an infectious one.
